name: Brazil

system.type: Two-round popular vote for president (absolute majority required)
system.eligibility: Voting compulsory for literate citizens 18–70; voluntary for illiterate, 16–17 and over-70s (IDEA)

wildFacts.text: Lula is the first president since Brazil's 1985 return to civilian rule to win after losing the first round.
A court extended voting nationwide by two hours on runoff day.
The winner was mathematically certain on election night.

notes: The runoff result is confirmed by two sources: the TSE and BBC, plus The Guardian (https://www.theguardian.com/world/ng-interactive/2026/oct/25/brazil-election-2026-live-second-round-results). Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round on 4 October 2026, according to BBC Brasil (https://www.bbc.com/portuguese/articles/cqe8rekpg9lxo). Turnout was 80.78% (abstention 19.22%), per the TSE results app. Voting is compulsory, per International IDEA (https://www.idea.int/data-tools/data/voter-turnout-database/compulsory-voting). Congress seat totals are not shown because they could not be verified. Per-state winners could not be verified, so the map shows the country as a whole.
